full_judgment:
Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 10-10-2018 passed by learned District Judge, Madaripur in Civil Revision No.14 of 2017 affirming judgment and order dated 5-7-2017 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur in Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 2014 having arises out of order dated 12-6-2017 passed by the same Court in Title Suit No. 124 of 2006 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 3. The suit was posted for peremptory hearing and on 12-6-2014 the petitioners sought adjournment which was rejected and the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit as plaintiffs failed to pay the cost ordered by the Court on 4-3-2014. The petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 2014 wherein defendant Nos.1-6 filed petition for recording abatement and consequently the case is abated vide order dated 5-7-2017 as the property is enlisted in 'Ka' schedule under Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001. 

 4. The revisional Court in Civil Revision No.24 of 2017 affirmed the judgment and order passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2014 abating the case. 

 6. Mr Probir Halder, learned Advocate assisted by Advocate Ms. Joya Bhattacharjee submits that the suit property is not vested property as the opposite party Nos.1-6 earlier got decree on 9-4-1981 in Title Suit No.470 of 1980 for declaration of title as well as other reliefs and Government's Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 1982 having filed for setting aside the ex-partee decree has also been dismissed-on 13-7-1985 and consequently said property has been released from vested property and opposite parties' name has been mutated and, as such, provision of section 13(1)(ka) will not be applicable in the instant case but both the Courts below failed to advert that legal provision and thereby arrived at a wrong conclusion. Mr Halder next submits that applicability of section 13 of the Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 depends upon sections 6 of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 which stipulates that no property can be enlisted as vested property regarding which competent Court passed judgment and decree and, as such, order of abatement having recorded in respect of the miscellaneous case is not sustainable in law. He further submits that if any property is declared as not vested property or if title is declared by any competent Court in that case, prottorpon of the suit land in favour of the owner is not proper prayer rather release of property from the list can be sought under section 10(4) of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001. Learned advocate further submits that in section 2 (neo) of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 the list of property to be included in the restoration list has been mentioned and, as such, the case property having not vested property, the provision of section 13 for passing order of abatement is not sustainable. He argued that the petitioners filed Title Suit No.124 of 2006 impleading the present opposite parties as defendants praying for declaration of title by adverse possession and confirmation of possession and, as such, there is no impediment to proceed with the suit as filed by the plaintiffs-petitioners but both the Courts below failed to appreciate that vital aspect of the case and erroneously passed order of abatement in Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 2014. 

 7. Mr Syed Aktarul Islam, learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No.2 submits that the petitioners' father was defendant No.7 in Title Suit No.470 of 1980 having filed by the predecessor of the present opposite parties seeking declaration of title and further declaration that the suit property is not vested and non-resident property and granting settlement of the said property is illegal and as petitioners' father has no claim in the suit land he refrained from contesting the suit by filing written statement and, as such, the suit has been decreed in favour of the opposite parties and now they have filed vexatious suit with a view to cause loss to the opposite parties. He further submits that the present petitioners without invoking the provision of special law filed suit under general provisions of law and, as such, the said suit is not maintainable as there exists special law having special provision for restoration or releasing the suit property if any lawful claim is there and, as such, the present suit filed by the petitioners is not sustainable and order passed by the Courts below cannot be interfered with. He further submits that restoration and release are interchangeable terms, although the opposite parties initiated proceeding for releasing property which also will be deemed as restoration of property alternatively in favour of the opposite parties and, as such, the said terms also broadly come within the purview of section 13 of the vested property restoration Ain, 2001. Learned advocate further submits that the petitioners sought declaration of title but in earlier suit the predecessor of the present petitioners was defendant No.7 wherein same matter has been considered by the Court which declared title in favour of the predecessor of the opposite parties and, as such, the present vexatious suit filed by the petitioners is not maintainable. Learned advocate further submits that the present proceeding is barred by the principle of approbation and reprobation as the present petitioners relying upon the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.470 of 1980 to that effect that the suit property is not vested and non resident property but they are denying the title of the opposite parties which has been passed in the same suit and, as such, the present proceeding is also not maintainable by the principle of approbation and reprobation. Learned advocate further submits that the present suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, although the suit has been abated by the Courts below, but alternatively the suit is also not maintainable by the principle of resjudicata and, as such, it is futile exercise to proceed with the suit and miscellaneous proceeding and it should be buried at its inception. 

 8. Learned advocate in support of his contention referred the case of Managing Director, Rupali Bank Ltd. and others vs Tafazal Hossain and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260, Abdul Jalil and others vs Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd. and other reported in 53 DLR (AD) 12, Parveen Banu @ Purnima and others vs Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, represented by its Chairman and others 42 DLR (AD) 234, Commissioner of Customs, Chittagong vs Giasuddin Chowdhuly and another 50 DLR (AD) 129, Osman Gani Mondal vs Mainuddin Ahmed and others reported in 27 DLR 61, Gopinath Das and others vs Government of Bangladesh and others 64 DLR 167, Burmah Easstern Employees Union and others 18 DLR 709, Nurul Hague (Md) and another vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Communications, railway Division and others 51 DLR (AD) 140, Jogesh Chandra Datta vs Government of Bangladesh and others 30 DLR 219 and the KK Modi vs KN Modi and others 3 Supreme Court Cases (1998) 573 in support of his contention. 

 9. Having gone through the revisional application, annexures and other materials it appears that original suit being Civil Suit No. 124 of 2006 filed by the predecessor of the present petitioners before the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Madaripur was dismissed for default on 12-3-2014 which was for declaration of title and confirmation of possession impleading predecessor of present opposite parties as defendant. Thereafter the present petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2014 before the same Court for restoration of original suit under order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in the said case the present opposite parties by filing an application prayed for recording abatement of the case as the suit property in question has been enlisted in the 'Ica' schedule under section 13 of the Vested property Prottorpon Ain 2001 and upon hearing the application, learned Senior Assistant Judge by order dated 5-7-2017 recorded abatement contending that the property in question has been enlisted in 'Ica' list under section 13 of Arpita Shampatty Prottarpon Ain, 2001 and the revisional Court also affirmed the judgment and order passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge. 

 11. Now the question arises whether the suit property is vested property or not. If the suit property is vested property in that case section 13(1) of the Ain will come into play and if any suit is pending, then it will be abated upon application by any party or automatically but if any property is declared to be not vested property, then it cannot be enlisted as Prottarponjoggo Shampatty under schedule 'Ka' under section 6 of the Ain. 

 12. In the instant case it appears that earlier in Title Suit No. 470 of 1980 civil Court declared title in favour of the opposite parties and the civil Court also declared that leasing out the suit land treating the same as enemy property is illegal and subsequently miscellaneous case filed by the government being Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 1982 for setting aside the said ex-parte decree was also dismissed by the said Court and, as such, it is clearly apparent that the said property is not vested property and, as such, it cannot be enlisted in the Prottarponjoggo Shampatty list under section 13 of the Ain. Section 2 (neo) of the Ain 2001 also defined the list of Prottarponjoggo Shampatty wherein it is clearly mentioned that if any property is to be treated vested property it is to be under the custody of the government but admittedly the property in question is not under custody of the Bangladesh government having admitted by both the parties. Since it is found that the suit property is not vested property it cannot be enlisted under section 13(1) of the Prottarponjoggo Shampatty list and it is also clearly apparent from the proceeding initiated by the opposite parties that they initiated proceeding not for restoration of the property but releasing the property under section 13(2)(a) and section 6 of the said Act and they got order of release having affirmed by the appellate tribunal and, as such, it is conspicuously clear that learned Assistant Judge failed to advert that provisions of law and erroneously passed order for abating the case. Regarding the submission of the learned advocate for the opposite party that earlier in Title Suit No. 470 of 1980 title of the opposite party has been declared and, as such, the present petitioner cannot claim title again over the self same suit property and the said suit is not maintainable, but regard being had to facts of the case, the said submission is not applicable in the present case as because order has been passed regarding abatement citing a prevalent law. He can ventilate grievance for such assertion in separate forum under appropriate provisions of law. Regarding the submission of the learned advocate the present proceeding is barred by the principle of approbation and reprobation, but the said principle is also not applicable in the instant case as because the instant matter is whether the Courts below passed order as per law, abating the case. Learned advocate intended to show that the petitioners are trying to rely on portion of the judgment of earlier suit that the property is not vested property but the petitioners by denying title of the opposite parties have filed the title suit which they are not entitled but such question is also not the matter of consideration in the instant proceeding as because instant proceeding is to be considered under the perimeters of vested property and Restoration Ain 2001 and since under section 6 of the vested property restoration Ain bars enlisting any property in the vested property list the said principle is not also applicable here. The opposite parties have got ample opportunity to make such submission if the original suit is restored to its file and number. 

 13. Consequently the decision referred by the learned Counsel for the opposite parties are not applicable in the instant case.
